description:
The Rust CI script runs its test suite in one temporary directory of its own and removes it when the run ends, so temporary files left by killed tests never outlive the run.

## Background

`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` already makes its work directory with `mktemp -d` and removes it on exit, but the test processes it starts inherit the caller's `TMPDIR`. Each test creates its own temporary directory, which the `tempfile` crate removes only when the test ends normally. A test killed by a per-test timeout, a cancelled run or a crash leaves its directory behind in the shared temporary directory.

On 2026-11-04 this left 31,970 stale `.tmp*` directories in a 32 GB tmpfs `/tmp`, exhausting its 1M inodes while 14 GB of space remained. Every test that creates many small files then failed with `No space left on device`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every test, doctest and build step `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` runs sees a `TMPDIR` that is a directory created for that run inside the caller's temporary directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: When the run exits, whether it passes, fails, is interrupted or is killed by a signal it can trap, that directory and everything under it is removed.
- [hard] REQ-03: The CI script's self-test shows that a file a test leaves in its temporary directory is gone after the run, including after a failing run.
- [hard] REQ-04: The script header and the CI gate description state that the run owns and removes its temporary directory.

## Notes

Long-lived daemons a run starts, such as a compiler cache server, must not inherit the per-run directory, because it disappears when the run ends; start them outside it or with their own temporary directory.
title: CI runs own and remove their temporary directory
